problem.title: Prime Ideals and Coordinate-Ring Maps of $R(\alpha,\beta)$
problem.statement: Let $k$ be an uncountable algebraically closed field, let $\alpha,\beta$ be algebraically independent over its prime subfield, and let $$R=R(\alpha,\beta)=k\langle x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4\rangle/(f_1,\ldots,f_6),$$ where $$\begin{aligned}f_1&=x_1(\alpha x_1-x_3)+x_3(x_1-\alpha x_3),&f_2&=x_1(\alpha x_2-x_4)+x_3(x_2-\alpha x_4),\\f_3&=x_2(\alpha x_1-x_3)+x_4(x_1-\alpha x_3),&f_4&=x_2(\alpha x_2-x_4)+x_4(x_2-\alpha x_4),\\f_5&=x_1(\beta x_1-x_2)+x_4(x_1-\beta x_2),&f_6&=x_1(\beta x_3-x_4)+x_4(x_3-\beta x_4).\end{aligned}$$ Is the augmentation ideal $R_+$ the only nontrivial graded prime ideal of $R$, and does $R$ admit no nontrivial map to a twisted homogeneous coordinate ring?
problem.background:
Collected from Oberwolfach Reports, which document mathematical workshops and their open-problem discussions.

**Source report:** [Interactions between Algebraic Geometry and Noncommutative Algebra (2010), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2010/22, pp. 1319--1381](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2010/22)

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** open

**Assessment.** The augmentation-ideal and twisted-homogeneous-coordinate-ring assertions are stated as conjectures in the source, and no general primary resolution was found.

**Sources checked.**

- [Rogalski--Sierra](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.0737)

problem.original_statement: Let k be an uncountable algebraically closed field and let R=R(\alpha,\beta)=k\langle x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4\rangle/(f_1,\ldots,f_6) be the birationally commutative GK-dimension-4 algebra defined by f_1=x_1(\alpha x_1-x_3)+x_3(x_1-\alpha x_3),\ f_2=x_1(\alpha x_2-x_4)+x_3(x_2-\alpha x_4),\ f_3=x_2(\alpha x_1-x_3)+x_4(x_1-\alpha x_3),\ f_4=x_2(\alpha x_2-x_4)+x_4(x_2-\alpha x_4),\ f_5=x_1(\beta x_1-x_2)+x_4(x_1-\beta x_2),\ f_6=x_1(\beta x_3-x_4)+x_4(x_3-\beta x_4) for algebraically independent \alpha,\beta. Is the augmentation ideal R_+ the only nontrivial graded prime ideal of R, and does R admit no nontrivial map to any twisted homogeneous coordinate ring?
